rationale: This is a tiny 128-line C++ program (14 functions, ~3.3 KB text) dominated by main (~1.9 KB) with a small Garage class, so cheap, broadly applicable passes get the highest security/diversity weights: SUB and SPLIT add strong instruction-level resistance with negligible runtime/size/risk, making them the backbone. FLA gets a solid security weight to flatten the large main function (the primary reverse-engineering target) but with a moderate RuntimeCost weight so hot loops inside main aren't aggressively rewritten; BCF gets slightly lower weights with elevated SizeCost since bogus control flow inflates an already small binary quickly. IBR is encouraged moderately for main's dispatch-heavy code but held back by a 0.5 RuntimeCost weight due to per-branch indirection overhead. ICALL gets balanced security/diversity with a 0.4 CorrectnessRisk because indirecting calls in C++ code with constructors and member functions can disturb ABI-sensitive call sites. IGV is left at low weights (still enabled) because the program has few globals and its initializer (_GLOBAL__sub_I_garage.cp) offers little obfuscation surface, so it will only apply where global-variable features strongly favor it.
